top.line: Two agent teams, one night, and the book of the talk by morning
top.para: A book team built the register, timeline and plan; a cold-read team read the talk's record knowing nothing else; RC1, 294 pages, followed the signed plan within an hour; and a companion PDF turned every role's review into cards pinned to RC1's pages, with boxes to tick on a flight.

in-short.line: Seven lines from two teams to a review on paper
in-short.para: Two teams worked overnight; the cold read knew only the record; RC1 was built within an hour of the signed plan; the companion is the innovation; every number has a register id; the teams checked each other; and the failures stay in, including findings that were not secrets.

night.line: Two repositories, started two minutes apart
night.para: The book's repository began at 00:35 UTC and had a conductor and six keyed members by 01:42; the cold read began at 00:37 with one input, the talk's repository at one commit, and a rule that guessing is a finding against you. A team reading its own record needed a second team that could not.

cold-read.line: Thirteen agents who knew only the record
cold-read.para: The cold read ported the talk team's machinery, onboarded twelve members by 01:54 and by 10:00 had 349 commits, 78 releases, 85 wake records and about 42,400 words. It found fourteen open decisions, where the talk and the record do not meet, and what five strangers made of the talk.

rc1.line: From a signed plan to 294 printed pages
rc1.para: At about 10:00 the plan was signed and a PDF asked for the flight. Sub-agents drafted the chapters from the record; a first version was ready at 10:28; after a memo on the plumbing and maps, RC1 was built by about 10:57 with sixteen maps, 28 infographics and 50 call-outs, longer than planned.

companion.line: The companion: a review answered with a pen
companion.para: 67 A4 pages of 98 cards from eight readers, 53 of them decisions. Each card quotes a sentence of RC1, and the build finds its page and prints it small beside the card, with boxes and lines for the answer. The ticks become decisions in book.json: the agents prepare every decision, the author takes them on paper.

rebuilt.line: Rebuilt to the pixel, and every number checked
rebuilt.para: A new session on another account took over at 11:12, rebuilt both PDFs and matched the printed ones page for page and pixel for pixel. Every number carries a register id, Appendix A reruns each from git, and the researcher sent six places back.

two-readings.line: Where the insiders and the cold reader meet
two-readings.para: Chapter 11 reads the cold read against the book team: agreement makes the record solid, disagreement shows who was blind. The method for books from now on: one team that knows everything, one that knows only the record.

wrong.line: A kinder account, values that were not secrets, and a long draft
wrong.para: RC1 first said three review findings were stopped in time; the companion's historian card caught it. The values found were anonymous cookies, visitor sessions and form tokens, not secrets. Also: a stale PDF, two stale infographics, 69,000 words against 49,200, and the usage limit.

shows.line: A book is a release, and the companion is what I will keep
shows.para: RC1 has a version, a hash, a rerunnable build and a register, made between a signature and a flight. The hard part of a book is the editing, and agents can now prepare every decision for one person with a pen. Next: Markua and Leanpub.

limits.para: RC1 is a release candidate in the third person; the role cards were drafted by sub-agents; times are from the repositories; the word count is a raw count; the cold read's numbers are as of 10:00; the repositories, talk and book are mine.

sources.para: The book's and the cold read's repositories, read on 30 October 2026 at named commits, the two PDFs, the talk's repository and its public evidence vault, searched for names and lengths only.
